scope: Eight real Samba AD/GMAC/BC/Direct/Java21 profiles: native GSS TGT key sizes 16/32, owned/borrowed connections, signing/GCM. Adds client cached-ticket expiration rejection, retained existing-open I/O and fresh retry to the existing concurrent-binding/replacement/reauthentication acceptance.
expiry_boundary: The test copies a genuine native TGT into a KerberosTicket with expired Java cache timestamps. It temporarily replaces Subject private credentials with that expired copy, excluding keys/tickets that could silently refresh it.
The encrypted ticket payload itself is unchanged; this is not a server-side expired AP-REQ test. The GSS mechanism rejects before any SESSION_SETUP is transmitted.

The original Subject credentials are restored in finally and the expired copy is destroyed. Existing SMB session/channel key and preauthentication state are retained; same-open I/O succeeds before fresh reauthentication. The real peer then accepts renewed authentication, later replacement binding and more reauthentications.
A second complete eight-profile run adds the explicit no-suppressed-disposal-error assertion. Reported totals describe this final run, not both runs combined.
